mode: CONFIRMATORY (pre-registered before any AF2 result was read)
research_question: When the attribute family choice is a genuine statistical decision (Poisson vs COM-Poisson nu=2 count columns), how often does automatic selection recover the true family, and how much of the Z-recovery loss from misspecification does it prevent?
lineage: E-consistent per-column + PR #129 generic model (experimental prototype; not adoptable for the manuscript)

pr129.local_change: opt-in train_mask pass-through in run_em_generic, run_generic_exploration, run_generic_hybrid

data.tau_source: PR #129: Gaussian tau_real_mixed = 1; COUNT calibration value 2.0 (label 'EASY' there; chosen here because the count columns then carry a strong latent signal)

candidates.failed_candidate_rule: PR #129: the Auto fit stops (SelectorStop); no other candidate wins by default

methods.wrong: Poisson <-> CMP2 swap on every count column
methods.support_only: PR #129 rule: first admissible candidate (poisson on every count column)
methods.note: support_only equals the one-directional misspecification (CMP2 columns as Poisson); wrong misspecifies all six count columns

primary_metric: Procrustes RMSE(Z) of the joint posterior mode (E1 evaluator)

interval.type: percentile bootstrap of the mean of replicate-level contrasts

secondary_metrics: true-family recovery per column (count columns, by true family)
missing_and_failure_rule: FAILED fits and non-OK modes are kept, never retried or imputed; contrasts only where both members are OK, exclusions counted next to every summary, together with failure rates. Success-only accuracy is always reported with the failure rate.
technical_stop_conditions: a test pair inside any train mask
Auto refit train mask differing from the cell's train mask
